title: Two Coworkers Discuss Job Security After a Company Merger
script: Farah: [thoughtful] Yoga, did you see the merger announcement? They're combining our department with the other office next month.
Yoga: I saw it this morning. Everyone's already whispering about layoffs, even though nothing official has been confirmed yet.
Farah: [gently] Exactly, and that uncertainty is somehow worse than bad news itself. At least bad news gives you something concrete to plan around.
Yoga: That's true. Waiting without answers has a specific kind of exhaustion, doesn't it, even though technically nothing bad has happened yet.
Farah: [reflective] I keep refreshing my email every ten minutes, as if checking constantly could somehow change whatever decision they've already made internally.
Yoga: I used to do that too, during the last restructuring. It never actually helped, it just kept my anxiety running at full speed all day.
Farah: [honestly] So what did help, if refreshing your email constantly didn't?
Yoga: Honestly, remembering that Allah already knows the outcome, even while it's still unknown to us, which sounds obvious but genuinely shifted something for me.
Farah: [calmly] I believe that too, in theory, but applying it while my rent is due next week feels considerably harder than believing it in general.
Yoga: Fair point. Belief doesn't cancel practical stress, it just gives the stress somewhere honest to land instead of spiraling endlessly.
Farah: [encouraging] What does that actually look like for you day to day, though, beyond just a comforting idea?
Yoga: Practically, I update my resume quietly, keep doing my job well, and try not to let fear make decisions faster than the facts require.
Farah: [carefully] Despite how sensible that sounds, part of me still wants a guarantee, some promise that everything will work out fine regardless.
Yoga: Nobody gets that guarantee, Farah, whether they trust Allah or not. The only real choice is what we do with the uncertainty we're already carrying.
Farah: [sincere] When you put it that way, refreshing my email seems like a fairly useless use of that uncertainty.
Yoga: Maybe update your resume instead, just in case, and then let the rest sit where it actually belongs, outside your control.
